reason: The hypothesis proposes laser cladding of AlCrTiZrMo, but the cited evidence describes a different deposition method (Co-FCVAD) for this alloy and laser cladding only for a different HEA (AlCoCrFeNi+WC). No cited evidence supports the formation of ZrTiO4, the specific hardness increase, or performance at 800 °C under thermal shock for this coating.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit AlCrTiZrMo HEA coatings
AlCrTiZrMo HEA forms a protective oxide layer (e.g., ZrTiO4) upon annealing
The HEA coating provides high hardness and wear resistance
The coating improves oxidation resistance in aggressive environments
The coating remains effective up to ~800 °C under thermal shock and corrosion
